name: Jewelry / watch / accessories
summary: Understated rings, chains and watches to finish an outfit; rich in history, with no attractiveness trials.
lead: Minimal jewelry, watches and other accessories are used in style communities to polish an outfit and signal taste or status without much effort. Common items include rings, necklaces, bracelets and wristwatches.

name: Grooming routine (nails, ear/nose hair)
summary: Keeping nails and ear and nose hair tidy; basic upkeep with no attractiveness trials.
lead: A grooming routine covering nails and ear and nose hair is a set of basic upkeep habits discussed in appearance communities as raising perceived polish. It sits at the line between hygiene and appearance.

name: Skin-care baseline routine
summary: Cleanser, moisturiser and SPF: the dull trio that dermatology guidance treats as the base layer, with sunscreen carrying most of the evidence.
lead: The skin-care baseline routine is the minimal regimen of gentle cleansing, moisturising and daily sun protection that many appearance-focused communities treat as the foundation before any active ingredients, procedures or other interventions are added.

name: Style subreddit / fit-check culture (r/malefashionadvice)
summary: Post a fit pic, get strangers' feedback: a free outfit-critique loop with no research on whether it moves the needle.
lead: Style subreddit fit-check culture is the practice of posting photographs of one's outfit to an online community and asking for feedback. The best-known example is r/malefashionadvice, a Reddit community where men share outfits and ask for style advice.

name: Style AI apps / virtual try-on
summary: Apps that preview outfits or looks on your own photo; handy for browsing, with no evidence on how well previews match reality.
lead: Style AI apps and virtual try-on tools are software that let a user preview clothing, accessories or hairstyles on a photo, video feed or avatar of themselves, and in some cases suggest outfits or looks automatically. Appearance communities discuss them as a way to test a style before buying or committing to it.

name: Hairstyle simulators / AI haircut preview
summary: Preview a haircut on your own selfie before committing; useful for ideas, with no data on how closely previews match results.
lead: Hairstyle simulators, including AI haircut preview tools, are apps and websites that overlay or generate a hairstyle on a user's photo so they can see a cut on their own face before visiting a stylist.

name: Testosterone gel (AndroGel)
summary: Prescription skin-applied testosterone for diagnosed low T; well studied in hypogonadal men, not a cosmetic product.
lead: Testosterone gel is a prescription topical form of testosterone replacement therapy applied to the skin, sold under brand names including AndroGel, Testim, TestoGel and Fortesta. It is prescribed mainly for male hypogonadism, in which the body produces too little testosterone, and is also used in masculinising hormone therapy for transgender men.

name: Nasal testosterone (Natesto)
summary: Prescription testosterone nasal gel for diagnosed low T; small studies suggest it may keep sperm and gonadotropins intact, but not a cosmetic product.
lead: Natesto is a prescription testosterone nasal gel used for testosterone replacement in men with hypogonadism. Wikipedia lists it as the intranasal testosterone product, supplied as a metered spray.

name: Oral testosterone undecanoate (Jatenzo / Kyzatrex)
summary: Prescription capsules that deliver testosterone by mouth for diagnosed deficiency; a medical TRT option, not a studied looksmaxxing tool.
lead: Oral testosterone undecanoate is a testosterone replacement therapy taken by mouth as a capsule. Testosterone undecanoate is a prodrug of testosterone, meaning it is converted to the active hormone in the body . Brand names include Jatenzo, Kyzatrex and Tlando in the United States, and Andriol elsewhere .

name: Testosterone pellets (Testopel)
summary: Rice-grain testosterone implants placed under the skin for months-long TRT; an established medical option with observational and small-trial data.
lead: Testosterone pellets are small cylindrical implants of crystalline testosterone placed under the skin to provide sustained hormone release. Testopel is the branded product; a 2012 multi-institution study notes that the FDA approved implantable testosterone pellets in 1972 for testosterone deficiency syndrome, and that clinical use was limited until Testopel was reintroduced .

name: Testosterone undecanoate injection (Aveed)
summary: Long-acting testosterone depot injection given in a clinic every few months; approved for deficiency, with a REMS programme for lung oil-embolism and anaphylaxis risk.
lead: Testosterone undecanoate injection is a long-acting intramuscular testosterone preparation marketed as Aveed in the United States and Nebido in Europe . It is a prodrug of testosterone used for replacement therapy in adult men with low or absent endogenous testosterone .

name: Sustanon (testosterone blend)
summary: A blend of four testosterone esters in oil, marketed as Sustanon 250; discussed in bodybuilding circles, with no appearance trials behind it.
lead: Sustanon is the brand name for blended testosterone ester injectables. Sustanon 250 contains four esters (propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate), while Sustanon 100 contains three (propionate, phenylpropionate and isocaproate) .

name: Cabergoline
summary: A prescription dopamine agonist that lowers prolactin; well studied for prolactinomas, discussed online as an add-on to hormone regimens, with documented heart-valve concerns at high doses.
lead: Cabergoline is an ergoline-derived dopamine D2 receptor agonist taken orally, sold under brand names such as Dostinex and Cabaser . The US drug label lists its indication as hyperprolactinemic disorders, either idiopathic or due to pituitary adenomas .

name: FSH / Menopur (HMG)
summary: Fertility gonadotropins (FSH, hMG) from IVF medicine, discussed in TRT circles as a way to keep sperm production going; the evidence is in women's fertility, not appearance.
lead: Menotropin, also called human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG), is a fertility drug extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women, whose urine is rich in FSH and LH . Menopur, made by Ferring, is a highly purified preparation; earlier products included Pergonal .

name: Fenugreek
summary: A culinary seed sold as an herbal testosterone and libido supplement; small trials of branded extracts report modest hormone changes, but evidence is limited.
lead: Fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum) is an annual legume native to the Near East and Mediterranean whose seeds and leaves are widely used as a spice and herb, particularly in South Asian cooking . It has a long history in traditional medicine, including documented use in ancient Egypt and Greek and Indian medicine .
claims: A herbal pill for more testosterone sounds like a cope
Fenugreek is only useful for specific problems such as erectile or digestive issues

name: D-aspartic acid (DAA)
summary: An amino acid sold as a testosterone booster; early work suggested a hormonal role, but trials in trained men found no increase and, at higher intake, a decrease.
lead: D-aspartic acid (DAA) is the D-enantiomer of aspartic acid, one of two D-amino acids commonly found in mammals; it is largely not used to build proteins and is found in tissues including the pituitary gland and testes . It is sold as a dietary supplement marketed for raising testosterone, particularly to men who lift weights.

name: Horny goat weed (Epimedium)
summary: A Chinese medicinal herb sold as a libido and erection supplement; its flavonoid icariin inhibits PDE5 in the lab, but human trial evidence is minimal.
lead: Horny goat weed is the common English name for plants of the genus Epimedium (family Berberidaceae), most of which are native to China . The Chinese name yin yang huo is rendered literally as lascivious goat herb . Traditional Chinese medicine has used it as a tonic for kidney yang deficiency, including low libido and fatigue .

name: Maca root
summary: An Andean root vegetable sold as a libido and energy supplement; a small number of trials suggest possible benefit for sexual desire, with limited evidence overall.
lead: Maca (Lepidium meyenii) is a biennial plant of the cabbage family cultivated at 4,000 to 4,500 meters in the central Andes of Peru, grown for its fleshy hypocotyl-taproot . Archaeological evidence shows cultivation around Lake Junín from about 1700 BC, and Spanish chroniclers described it in the early 1600s . Commercial interest grew from the late 1980s, driven by its purported effect on fertility .

name: Panax ginseng
summary: A classic East Asian adaptogen root sold for energy, libido and testosterone; a Cochrane review found small, likely not clinically meaningful effects on erectile function.
lead: Panax ginseng, also called Asian, Chinese or Korean ginseng, is a perennial plant native to mountainous areas of the Russian Far East, northeast China and the Korean peninsula; its root is the original source of ginseng and is harvested after five or six years of cultivation . It is used in folk and traditional medicine as a tonic .

name: Mucuna pruriens
summary: A tropical bean rich in natural L-DOPA, used in Ayurveda and sold as a dopamine, libido and testosterone supplement; human evidence exists mainly for Parkinson's disease.
lead: Mucuna pruriens, the velvet bean, is a tropical climbing legume native to Africa and tropical Asia, grown as forage and green manure and eaten in parts of Indonesia . Its seeds contain about 3 to 6 percent L-DOPA (levodopa), the dopamine precursor used in Parkinson's disease treatment, while its pod hairs contain compounds that cause intense itching .
claims: Mucuna pruriens is a way to "dopamine max" because it contains L-DOPA
Mucuna boosts libido and male fertility

name: DIM (diindolylmethane)
summary: A broccoli-derived compound sold as an estrogen-metabolism supplement; the appearance and hormone claims are mostly untested in humans.
lead: 3,3'-Diindolylmethane (DIM) is a compound formed in the body from indole-3-carbinol, which occurs in cruciferous vegetables such as broccoli, Brussels sprouts, cabbage and kale. It is sold as a dietary supplement .

name: Calcium-D-glucarate
summary: A glucaric acid salt sold to help the body clear estrogen; the evidence is mostly rodent work from the 1980s and 90s.
lead: Calcium D-glucarate is a salt of glucaric acid (saccharic acid), a sugar acid that occurs naturally in fruits and vegetables. Glucarate salts are used in dietary supplements as precursors to D-glucaro-1,4-lactone, described as an inhibitor of the enzyme beta-glucuronidase .

name: Chrysin
summary: A passionflower and honey flavone sold as a weak aromatase inhibitor; poorly absorbed orally and no evidence it affects testosterone.
lead: Chrysin (5,7-dihydroxyflavone) is a flavone, a type of flavonoid, found in honey, propolis, passionflowers (Passiflora species), Scutellaria baicalensis and some mushrooms and fruits . It is an ingredient in some dietary supplements .
claims: Chrysin is a natural aromatase inhibitor that raises testosterone.

name: Nettle root
summary: Stinging nettle root extract, studied for prostate symptoms and promoted as an SHBG binder; the testosterone claim rests on lab work.
lead: Nettle root refers to extracts of the roots of Urtica dioica, the common stinging nettle. Root extracts have a long tradition in German phytotherapy for benign prostatic hyperplasia .
claims: Nettle root binds SHBG and raises free testosterone.

name: Test booster blends (Prime Male, TestoFuel)
summary: Multi-herb over-the-counter testosterone-booster products; no published trial of these specific products was found.
lead: Test booster blends are multi-ingredient dietary supplements marketed to increase or support testosterone, usually combining herbal extracts, vitamins and minerals. Brands such as Prime Male and TestoFuel are sold online and are discussed in forums on testosterone and looksmaxxing.

name: Desiccated beef testicle supplements
summary: Dried bovine testicle capsules sold on a 'like supports like' basis; the idea descends from 1889 organ-extract experiments later attributed to placebo.
lead: Desiccated beef testicle supplements are dried, usually encapsulated, preparations of bovine testicular tissue sold as dietary supplements. They are promoted within the 'like supports like' idea that consuming an organ benefits the same organ in the consumer.

name: Oxytocin nasal spray
summary: A bonding-hormone spray sold online; real social-neuroscience research behind the hormone, but no study backs it as a looks or ascension tool.
lead: Oxytocin is a peptide hormone of nine amino acids made mainly in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary. It acts on the uterus during labor, on the breast during lactation, and on brain circuits involved in social behaviour . A synthetic form is a standard obstetric drug given by infusion or injection .
claims: Oxytocin spray can fix social anxiety or the "ndpill" mindset.
Oxytocin from sex or relationships can be "nuked" or avoided by following specific routines.
Oxytocin supports bone growth, so it is relevant to facial structure.
Peptide spray kits combining oxytocin with other compounds are a convenient way to use these peptides.

name: Estradiol / HRT (feminising or menopause)
summary: The main estrogen, prescribed for menopause and feminising therapy; forum users also ask whether it affects skin, hair and body shape, with real medical risks attached.
lead: Estradiol (E2) is the principal estrogen sex hormone, a steroid made mainly by the ovaries and, in smaller amounts, by other tissues including in males through aromatisation of testosterone. It acts on estrogen receptors alpha and beta to regulate reproductive tissues, bone, skin, fat distribution and brain function .
claims: High estradiol protects hair follicles, so estradiol plus a DHT blocker can keep hair.
Estradiol levels should be tested because they matter for men's hormone health.
HRT is comparable to using steroids.

name: Combined oral contraceptive pill for acne
summary: Estrogen-plus-progestin birth control pills that the FDA has cleared for moderate acne in women who also want contraception; effective for many, with clotting risk attached.
lead: Combined oral contraceptive pills combine an estrogen with a progestin and are taken mainly to prevent pregnancy. Dermatologists also use them to treat acne in women because the hormonal changes they cause reduce sebum production .

name: Natural TRT / "enclo + hCG" protocols
summary: Non-testosterone ways of raising testosterone, such as enclomiphene and hCG, that aim to avoid shutting down fertility; discussed as TRT alternatives, with limited evidence.
lead: "Natural TRT" or "enclo + hCG" refers to protocols in which men aim to raise their own testosterone using drugs that stimulate the pituitary-testicular axis, rather than taking testosterone itself. Enclomiphene (enclomifene) is a nonsteroidal selective estrogen receptor modulator, the more antiestrogenic isomer of clomifene, and hCG is a gonadotropin that mimics LH .
